query: Characterize the anatomical localization and functional properties of the glyt2-gfra1a co-expressing molecular subtype. Plot 2D brain projections (dorsal and lateral views) showing the subtype's spatial distribution with brain region boundaries. Compare maximum visual stimulus response and swimming correlation across three groups (glyt2_gfra1a, other responsive, other non-responsive neurons) using violin plots with statistical significance testing. Show trial-by-trial calcium activity traces aligned to forward motion stimuli with simultaneous fictive swimming behavior.

analyse_plan.Objective: Identify the whole‑brain anatomical distribution of the glyt2–gfra1a molecular subtype, quantify its maximum response magnitude across 8 visual stimuli, extract its stimulus‑locked mean activity trace, and compare its functional properties with other responsive and non-responsive neuron groups using violin plots with statistical significance testing, to define its specific role in visual‑motor transformation.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify that the glyt2–gfra1a subtype meets cross‑animal replication criteria (present in all 3 fish, ≥5 cells per fish). Confirm that glyt2 and gfra1a positivity is defined by consistent RNA spot thresholds (≥25 spots each). Ensure maximum ΔF/F responses are computed across the full 8‑visual‑stimulus panel. Validate that violin plots use identical grouping criteria for max response and swim correlation analyses. Confirm statistical tests (Wilcoxon rank-sum) are applied correctly for pairwise group comparisons.
Steps:
1. Load Data: Import glyt2–gfra1a subtype membership, 3D spatial coordinates, brain region annotations, single-neuron ΔF/F traces, 8 visual stimulus time series, swimming correlation values, and trial-by-trial activity records from three fish.
2. Anatomical Mapping: Render 3D spatial distribution of the glyt2_gfra1a subtype on the whole‑brain atlas (dorsal/lateral views), highlighting hindbrain boundaries with colored dashed lines.
3. Response Quantification: Calculate the maximum ΔF/F response amplitude for each neuron across the full 8-visual-stimulus panel; group neurons into three categories: glyt2_gfra1a subtype, other visually responsive neurons, and other non-responsive neurons; generate violin plots comparing max ΔF/F across groups, and perform Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to assess statistical significance.
4. Activity Trace Analysis: Compute the mean stimulus-aligned calcium activity trace across all glyt2_gfra1a neurons, and extract trial-by-trial activity traces for Fish 2 aligned to forward motion stimuli.
5. Behavior Correlation: Compute Pearson correlation coefficients between each neuron's activity and fictive swimming; generate violin plots comparing correlation values across the three groups, with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for pairwise significance.
6. Save Key Results: Save the glyt2_gfra1a neuron 3D coordinate matrix (atlas-aligned), hindbrain subregion boundary coordinates (colored dashed lines), per-neuron max ΔF/F response vector (three groups), per-neuron swimming correlation coefficient vector (three groups), Wilcoxon rank-sum test raw p-values and significance labels (*, ns), violin plot color mapping (three groups: light blue), glyt2_gfra1a mean ΔF/F activity trace vector, Fish 2 trial-by-trial activity matrix (5 trials), fictive swimming behavior time series, forward motion stimulus time interval coordinates (pink shaded area), swim onset marker coordinates (green vertical lines), activity trace scale bar parameter (0.05 ΔF/F), 3D brain map scale bar parameter (100 μm), time axis calibration parameter (0–10 s corresponding frame count), and sample size label (n=3 fish).
7. Visualization: Integrate 3D anatomical maps, max response violin plot, swimming correlation violin plot, and trial-by-trial activity traces into a single unified panel, with statistical significance labels added to violin plots.

p<0.05 for significant comparisons (*); ns = not significant

key_analysis_results: The glyt2–gfra1a molecular subtype is exclusively localized to the caudal hindbrain (medulla oblongata). Violin plots show that glyt2_gfra1a neurons have significantly higher maximum ΔF/F responses to visual stimuli and stronger positive correlation with fictive swimming than both other responsive neurons and non-responsive neurons (p<0.05, Wilcoxon rank-sum test). Trial-by-trial activity traces from Fish 2 confirm consistent, stimulus-locked activation aligned with swim onset during forward visual motion.
key_analysis_conclusions: The glyt2–gfra1a co-expressing subtype represents a genetically defined, hindbrain‑localized neuronal population specialized for encoding forward visual motion and driving swimming behavior, serving as a core motor integrator node in the zebrafish optomotor response circuit.

summary_report.abstract: Fig_5E characterizes the glyt2–gfra1a motor integrator subtype: 3D whole‑brain maps show exclusive hindbrain localization; violin plots reveal significantly higher max visual responses and stronger swimming correlation than other neuron groups; trial-by-trial traces confirm consistent stimulus-locked activation aligned with swim onset, defining a key visual-motor circuit node.
summary_report.methods: Data were derived from three 6 dpf zebrafish with integrated whole‑brain calcium imaging and EASI‑FISH. The glyt2–gfra1a co-expressing subtype was identified using binary gene expression thresholds (≥25 spots each) and cross‑animal filtering. 3D anatomical distribution was rendered using mapZebrain atlas registration. Maximum ΔF/F responses were calculated for each neuron across 8 visual stimuli, and Pearson correlation coefficients between neuronal activity and fictive swimming were computed. Neurons were grouped into glyt2_gfra1a, other responsive, and other non-responsive categories. Violin plots were generated to compare max response and swim correlation across groups, with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for pairwise statistical significance. Trial-by-trial activity traces from Fish 2 were aligned to forward motion stimulus onset.
summary_report.results: The glyt2–gfra1a subtype is almost exclusively located in the caudal hindbrain (medulla oblongata) with no detectable presence in other brain regions. Violin plots demonstrate that glyt2_gfra1a neurons have significantly higher maximum ΔF/F responses (median ~0.3) than both other responsive neurons (median ~0.2) and non-responsive neurons (median ~0.1) (all p<0.05). Similarly, glyt2_gfra1a neurons show significantly stronger positive correlation with swimming (median ~0.2) than the other two groups. Trial-by-trial traces from Fish 2 show consistent, sharp activation peaks aligned with forward motion stimulus onset and swim onset markers, with minimal trial-to-trial variability.
summary_report.discussion: Fig_5E provides a complete single‑subtype characterization that exemplifies the WARP framework’s power: glyt2 (a marker for glycinergic inhibitory neurons) and gfra1a (a neurotrophic receptor) together define a functionally pure population dedicated to forward motion‑evoked swimming. Its exclusive caudal hindbrain localization places it in the motor-premotor region responsible for executing swim commands, rather than purely visual processing. The strong stimulus selectivity, behavior correlation, and statistical significance relative to other neuron groups establish this subtype as a minimal, genetically addressable component of the optomotor reflex. This level of resolution enables future targeted perturbation studies to directly test the causal role of this specific population in visual-motor behavior.

question: ﻿To characterize the anatomical localization, maximum visual stimulus response, mean calcium activity dynamics, and swimming behavior correlation of the glyt2–gfra1a co-expressing molecular subtype. Based on gene expression, 3D spatial coordinates, ΔF/F calcium traces, visual stimulus responses, and swimming correlation data from three cross‑animal validated fish, generate a multi‑panel visualization including 3D brain maps, violin plots comparing max response/swim correlation across three groups, and trial-by-trial activity traces aligned to forward motion stimuli.
